target.title: fix(cron): use direct lookup instead of paginated search in cron edit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When running the `openclaw cron edit` command to patch a schedule or payload, the CLI previously used `loadCronJobForEditSchedulePatch` to look up the existing cron job. This function was highly inefficient: it sequentially paginated through all cron jobs (using `cron.list` with up to 50 pages of 200 items each) to locate a single job by its ID.

This linear search (`O(N)`) is extremely slow for large gateway configurations, especially in environments with many cron jobs, and places unnecessary load on the gateway.

## Fix

Replace the paginated search loop in the CLI with a direct `O(1)` call to `readCronJobForEdit` (which invokes `cron.get`), fetching the single job by its ID in one step.

## Test plan

- Modified `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.test.ts` to mock `cron.get` instead of `cron.list` for the timeout-only edit test.
- Ran `register.cron-edit.test.ts` test suite, all 21 tests passed.


## Evidence

Passed tests on branch `fix/2.2-cron-edit-direct-lookup`:
